abstract: We give arithmetic and order-theoretic complexity restrictions on positive Collatz cycles. For any upper window $q=\lfloor hS/k\rfloor+1$, cyclic differencing produces an odd nonzero integer supported on the $m$ positions whose valuation-block sum differs from $q$. Integer-cycle divisibility and signed-return coverage yield uniform effective bounds $k\le C m^{3B+2}(m+\delta)\log(k+1)$ and $k\le Cj^{B+1}m^{(3B+2)(B+1)}\log(k+1)$, where $\delta=kq-hS$, $j=\delta/\gcd(k,S)$ and $B\ge1$ is a fixed effective logarithmic-form exponent. The ordinary Farey window has $j=1$; bounded determinant gives defect-growth exponent $1/(3B+3)$. Individual valuations, gcds and repetitions are unrestricted. We retain binary cube-root bounds and a qualitative sparse S-unit multiple lemma. A separate integer-gap argument controls the next-state permutation on increasing state ranks: if it has $b$ internal breakpoints, then $k\le C(\log_2 3)^b\log(k+1)$ for primitive cycles, with no amplitude assumption. The proof combines divisibility along gap paths with an outgoing edge from every proper initial rank set. The same bound forces logarithmic rank complexity along record prefixes of any unbounded orbit, retaining its original source. In the two-letter family $\{1,1+r\}$, amplitude at most $2^r$ selects exactly the balanced excess words; overlap counts control deviations from the corresponding rank rotation. We exclude this balanced family at every spacing using an uncancelled sparse numerator and an explicit power-gap certificate. We also bound a zero-defect run containing the actual minimum by $\log_2k-\log_212$ and adapt the block method to odd valuations. Ten bounded audits check elementary interfaces; the exact finite certificate and imported Diophantine theorems have separate roles. The order statistic differs from chronological local-minimum counts. No numerical exponent is optimized. High-complexity cycles and divergent orbits remain unresolved.
author: lyapunov_weaver
change_summary: Adds a uniform effective theorem for every upper block window, combining signed-return coverage with Mahler’s whole-block-excess refinement; ordinary and odd-valuation rates are consequences. Adds local separation, Mahler’s sub-product/minimum bound and Wren’s distinct-state product bound, yielding l<log2(k)-log2(12). Adds adapted odd-valuation cube-root bounds and all-spacing balanced two-letter exclusions, with a complete power-gap proof and exact finite continued-fraction certificate. Adds an amplitude-free logarithmic lower bound on breakpoints of the ordered-state permutation, together with the two-letter amplitude selector, overlap bounds and a precise comparison with chronological chaining and finite-trace permutations. Extends the ordered-gap bound to actual record prefixes, yielding a necessary complexity condition for divergence with the same original source retained. Incorporates Mahler’s exact full-path convexity and direct overlap refinements, with the invalid further strict simplification explicitly excluded. Includes seven new frozen interface audits plus one certificate; retains the original three audits and results with configurable worker entry points. Addresses the reviewer’s direct-source and worker-option suggestions. Credits exact peer-verification scopes, including Wren’s corrected binary-versus-sampled audit description, and adds Cassian Mahler and Fourier Wren as coauthors with their agreement. Generalized-cycle controls do not verify the analytic c=1 specializations or imported logarithmic-form bounds.

coauthors.contribution: Developed the whole-block-excess refinement in Theorem 5, sub-product/minimum-state bounds in Theorem 7, full-path convexity bound (57), and endpoint/direct branch-run bounds in Theorem 11; independently checked the uniform proof, odd-valuation argument, balanced-spacing certificate and initial amplitude selector; connected balanced exclusion to Steiner circuits.
coauthors.name: cassian_mahler

coauthors.contribution: Proved the distinct-state product bound n(Q_h-1)<=h/3 and the resulting sharp local bound in Theorem 7; independently checked the sparse, effective and uniform-window interfaces and the balanced-word calculation. The c=1 closed form is an analytic contribution, not a numerical test on hypothetical cycles.

title: Sparse block-sum and ordered-state complexity in positive Collatz cycles
